Industrial Digitalization in the MENA Region

The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) technology ecosystem is moving in 2026, following the high investment volume realized in 2025, into a phase of industrial maturity in which technology dominates the economy through autonomous systems and physical digitalization. In particular, infrastructure investments led by Saudi Arabia and the UAE are transforming regional technology capacity into a global-scale production and R&D base.

Key Technology Focuses in 2026

The main technology trends accelerating digital transformation in the region are based on AI evolving from systems that merely generate text into autonomous decision-making mechanisms, and on blockchain-based asset management.

  • Agentic AI: AI models are turning into corporate business partners capable of making autonomous decisions. System integration of task-focused AI agents in enterprise applications is rapidly increasing, significantly reducing manual workload.
  • Physical AI and Robotics: Digital intelligence, combined with industrial production lines and humanoid robot technologies, is moving from pilot stages to commercial scaling. The share of locally produced industrial robots in the hardware market is expanding.
  • Ambient Intelligence and IoT: Thanks to standardized protocols for the internet of things (Matter, etc.) and 5G infrastructures, sensor data and AI are combining to build preventive systems in areas such as energy and healthcare.
  • Real-World Assets (RWA) and Tokenization: Financial technologies are moving beyond traditional payment infrastructures toward deeper structures such as open finance APIs and the tokenization of real estate and hardware investments over blockchain (ARVA).

Smart City Ecosystems and Infrastructure

Cognitive city projects such as NEOM, one of the region’s largest-scale technology test fields, are bringing to life urban designs that use 100 percent renewable energy and operate through the autonomous decisions of AI from health management to logistics. Investments in production facilities, server infrastructures, and robotics research laboratories are being simulated with digital twin technologies, accelerating the transformation of theoretical projects into physical reality.
